text: This chunk provides an overview of Cholera, including its symptoms, causes, and historical context. It explains that Cholera is an acute diarrheal disease caused by the bacterium *Vibrio cholerae*, which can spread rapidly and lead to severe dehydration and shock. The text notes that while historically Cholera was highly fatal, it is now less severe and less common. The disease can affect all ages but is more prevalent in adults, particularly those over 15 years old. It is often found in areas with poor sanitation and is more common in certain regions like Southeast Asia, South Asia, Africa, and Latin America. The chunk also includes statistics on global Cholera cases and deaths as of 2010 and mentions the low incidence in Thailand in 2012.
